title: High Characteristic Voltage YBCO Josephson Junctions Written With a Focused Helium Ion Beam
summary: We report in-plane Josephson junctions written directly into YBa$_2$Cu$_3$O$_{7-δ}$ (YBCO) thin films with a focused helium ion beam (He FIB). The characteristic voltage $I_{\mathrm{C}}R$ of these junctions, where $I_{\mathrm{C}}$ is the Josephson critical current and $R$ is the junction resistance, sets the operating frequency and the sensitivity of the circuits built from them. A single line irradiation with a dose of \SI{500}{ions/nm} across a \SI{4}{\micro\metre} wide electrode produced a junction with $I_{\mathrm{C}}R$ of 929 \si{\micro\volt} at \SI{1.6}{K}, which is `higher than the 200 to 400 \si{\micro\volt} typical of junctions fabricated previously in our laboratory. Temperature dependent resistance, current-voltage characteristics, magnetic field modulation of the critical current, and Shapiro steps under 20.5~GHz microwave irradiation show Josephson behavior with an excess current below 5 percent of the critical current. The critical current falls steeply with temperature near the junction transition and saturates at low temperature. We attribute this behavior to a barrier at the metal insulator transition, where hopping conduction through localized states is active at finite temperature and freezes out on cooling. We describe the changes in surface preparation, sample selection, beam focusing, and sample storage that accompanied the improvement, although the present data do not separate their individual contributions. Larger characteristic voltages at these dimensions are an encouraging result for rapid single flux quantum and adiabatic quantum flux parametron logic and for superconducting quantum interference devices operating at elevated temperature.

title: Stabilization of LaH$_{10}$ with Thorium: Superconductivity in (La,Th)H$_{10}$ up to 232 K near 1 Mbar
summary: Ternary lanthanum-based hydrides are among the best high-temperature superconductors. Here we show that substituting La with thorium stabilizes La(Th)H$_{10}$ clathrate structure at $\sim$1 Mbar while only minimally suppressing superconductivity. The resulting cubic (La,Th)H$_{10}$ phase, synthesized from relatively air-stable La$_2$Th, La$_3$Th and La$_5$Th alloys, reaches an onset $\textit{T$_c$}$ = 232 K at 134 GPa, as confirmed by contact resistance measurements. Superconductivity was verified by two independent methods: electrical resistance and contactless radio-frequency measurements under applied magnetic fields at various pressures. Using a record-high pulsed current of 380 mA, we investigated critical phenomena in P6$_3$/mmc-(La,Th)H$_9$ at 173 GPa, which allowed for the experimental determination of a single superconducting gap within the s-wave model: $Δ(0) = 37 \pm 4.5$ meV and $2Δ(0)/kT_c = 4.9 \pm 0.6$. The La-Th-H system is chemically rich: in addition to the decahydride and nonahydride mentioned above, we also identified nanocrystalline I4/mmm-(La,Th)H$_4$ (5-6 nm grain size), (La,Th)H$_6$, as well as $hP13$, $cF80$ and $A15$ phases with compositions of (La,Th)H$_{5.75-6.25}$ and $\textit{T$_c$}$ $\approx$ 83 K at 70-80 GPa, and a possible (La,Th)H$_{16}$ polyhydride.

title: Phase diagram and lattice structure of interlayer vortices in multilayer Ising superconductors in parallel magnetic fields
summary: In this work, we investigate layered $s$-wave Ising superconductors under an in-plane magnetic field using self-consistent solutions of the microscopic Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations. Comparing bilayer, four-layer, and infinite-layer systems, we determine how the phase diagram and vortex structure evolve with layer number. Compared to standard Ginzburg-Landau treatments, our approach applies over a broader parameter regime and self-consistently resolves the spatial and layer dependence of the gap amplitude without prescribing its form. We find that the field range supporting the conventional Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) phase (defined as having no interlayer vortices) is reduced with increasing layer number and is essentially absent at nonzero magnetic flux in the infinite-layer system, consistent with recent thickness-dependent experiments on multilayer 2H-NbSe$_2$. In the infinite-layer limit, the Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov (FFLO) phase containing interlayer vortices persists to progressively larger in-plane fields as temperature is lowered below the zero-field critical temperature, consistent with the experimentally observed low-temperature enhancement of the upper critical field. The vortex structure also evolves with interlayer hopping: in four-layer systems, for the fluxes and system sizes considered, increasing hopping reorganizes vortices from outer to inner interlayer junctions. At larger hopping, the gap distortion associated with an interior vortex extends to the surface layers, producing gap suppression comparable to that in the interior layers. Representative six-layer calculations show that interior vortices likewise produce a finite, although weaker, modulation of the surface-layer gap. These results highlight layer number and interlayer tunneling as key parameters governing the phase diagram and vortex arrangement in multilayer Ising superconductors.

title: Sharp bounds on the Eliashberg critical temperature: a comparison principle, convexity in the spectrum, and the Kiessling-Altshuler-Yuzbashyan conjectures
comment: 23 pages, 2 figures. Lean 4 formalization of the finite-dimensional core, two computer-assisted certificates and all scripts are in the ancillary files
summary: In Eliashberg theory of phonon-mediated superconductivity with vanishing Coulomb pseudopotential, the critical temperature $T_c$ marks the linear instability of the normal state. Kiessling, Altshuler and Yuzbashyan (KAY) characterized it through the top eigenvalue of a compact operator on Matsubara-frequency sequences. They proved that $T_c$ is unique at strong coupling and conjectured $T_c<C(λ\langleω^2\rangle)^{1/2}$ for every coupling $λ$, with $\langleω^2\rangle$ the second moment of the normalized phonon spectrum and $C\approx0.1827$ sharp, a bound Leavens stated in 1977 on partly numerical grounds. A preprint by Kondratev, not yet peer reviewed, gives a proof of this bound and of all-coupling uniqueness. We give an independent proof, for every spectrum with finite second moment, based on a comparison principle that is also Kondratev's central step and was proved to first order by Bergmann and Rainer: strengthening the pairing interaction at every Matsubara transfer, strictly at the smallest one, strictly raises the top eigenvalue. At fixed $λ$ and $\langleω^2\rangle$ a single Einstein mode maximizes $T_c$. Convexity of the top eigenvalue in the spectrum gives sharp bounds on $T_c$ by the moments $\intω^nα^2F dω$, $0\le n\le1$, including Leavens's zeroth-moment bound $T_c\le c_0\intα^2F dω$, $c_0\approx0.231$ numerically, optimal at moderate coupling. All bounds persist under a Coulomb pseudopotential with symmetric cutoff. A prefix decomposition of non-increasing vectors proves a third KAY conjecture, not treated in the preprint. The finite-dimensional core, including that conjecture, is formalized in Lean 4, and two computer-assisted proofs independent of the comparison principle confirm the Einstein bound.

title: Magnon binding in a quantum Hall ferromagnet with a periodic electric field
summary: A spin wave in a filling-one quantum Hall ferromagnet is neutral but carries an electric dipole perpendicular to its momentum. A spatially periodic electrostatic potential therefore creates parallel channels for spin waves. We use this established mechanism to calculate how confinement changes the exchange binding of magnons travelling in the same direction. Narrower channels increase the overlap of their transverse wavefunctions and strengthen the effective attraction. In an isolated harmonic channel, the energy required to remove one magnon from a cluster of $N$ is $π(k_*\ell)^4N(N-1)/4$ times the transverse level spacing to leading order, where $k_*$ is the mean wave number along the channel and $\ell$ is the magnetic length. We predict the frequency and momentum dependence of the spectral line for adding a second magnon to one already present, both in an isolated channel and in a coupled array. Tunnelling in a wide array can make the binding energy exponentially small, while a strip narrower than the transverse pair size recovers one-dimensional binding at sufficiently weak attraction. We also find that a moving potential can carry a single wave packet with less spreading than free propagation when its initial group velocity matches the potential's speed.

title: Inversion of magnetization anisotropy in low magnetic fields for textured Bi2223 superconductor due to magnetic responses from superconducting crystallites and intercrystalline boundaries
summary: A detailed study of the magnetic anisotropy of a bulk textured high-temperature superconductor Bi2223 has been carried out. In the range of moderate and high fields (up to 1 kOe), the difference ΔM between the upper and lower branches of the magnetization hysteresis loop is larger when the external magnetic field H is parallel to the normal of the texturing plane (H||NTP) than when H is parallel to the texturing plane (H {\perp} NTP). This magnetic anisotropy is typical for such textured superconductors. However, at small values of the maximum applied field Hmax (up to 15 Oe at a temperature T = 78 K), an anomalous inversion of anisotropy has been found: ΔM(H||NTP) < ΔM(H {\perp} NTP). It has been established that in the field range up to ~30 Oe (the first penetration field into Bi2223 crystallites is about 30 Oe at T = 78 K), the magnetic hysteresis is determined only by the magnetic flux trapped in the intercrystallite boundary subsystem. The pronounced platelet shape of the Bi2223 crystallites leads to partial screening of the external field inside the sample when the field is oriented parallel to the crystallite c-axis. The observed inverse anisotropy ΔM(H||NTP) < ΔM(H {\perp} NTP) has been explained by the fact that the effective magnetic field into the intercrystallite boundaries is smaller for the H||NTP orientation than for H {\perp} NTP. Therefore, when the field is oriented H||NTP, a larger external field is required for magnetic flux to penetrate into the sample inner than for the H {\perp} NTP orientation.

title: Nonlinear spin generation and spin photocurrent as a symmetry and magnetic domain probe in unconventional magnets
summary: Unconventional magnets host momentum-dependent spin splitting without spin-orbit coupling. We demonstrate that the combination of nonlinear spin polarisation and spin photocurrent is a powerful diagnostic tool for probing the spin space group symmetry, magnetic domain, and quantum geometry in unconventional magnets, providing information beyond their equilibrium spin texture. We develop a mechanism-resolved joint symmetry analysis of second-order spin photoresponse tensors and analyse their frequency dependence, magnetic parity and relaxation scaling. We show that unconventional magnets are natural platforms to achieve large magnetic-even spin photocurrent induced by unpolarised light, making them promising candidates for polariser-free spin sources. We present numerical illustrations for prototypical hybrid parity and odd parity magnet models. Our work provides optical fingerprints connecting spin-space symmetry to distinct microscopic pathways of spin accumulation and transport.

title: Failure of Mean-Field Critical Scaling and Two Distinct Dissipation Regimes in La$_2$SmNi$_2$O$_{7-δ}$
summary: Recently, superconductivity with an onset transition temperature ($T_{\mathrm{c}}^{\mathrm{onset}}$) up to 96 K has been observed in the $\mathrm{La}_{2-x}\mathrm{Sm}_{1+x}\mathrm{Ni}_2\mathrm{O}_{7-δ}$ system under pressure, providing an attractive platform for investigating superconducting mechanisms in nickelates. Here, we systematically analyzed the critical scaling and vortex dynamics for the $\mathrm{La}_2\mathrm{Sm}\mathrm{Ni}_2\mathrm{O}_{7-δ}$ single crystal with $T_{\mathrm{c}}^{\mathrm{onset}}=92.5$ K under pressure. Within the Ullah--Dorsey framework, neither the two-dimensional nor three-dimensional scaling provides a good collapse near $T_{\mathrm{c}}^{\mathrm{MF}}$. This failure may be associated with the multiband composite order parameter of bilayer nickelates, in which pairing is mainly driven by antiferromagnetic exchange in the $d_{z^2}$ orbital, whereas the superfluid stiffness is mainly governed by the $d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbital. The two-step decrease in the logarithmic resistivity reveals two distinct dissipative regimes. The low-temperature regime is well described by the thermally assisted flux flow (TAFF) model, whereas the high-temperature regime cannot be explained by the vortex dynamics involved with the superconducting fluctuation. The crossover between the two regimes may be associated with the orbital-dependent evolution of vortex cores. These results suggest the significant role of the composite order parameter in critical fluctuations and vortex-motion dissipation in nickelates.

title: Chiral-phonon-mediated spin current injection into an Ising superconductor
summary: We theoretically propose chiral-phonon-mediated spin current injection into an Ising superconductor in a chiral-insulator/Ising-superconductor heterostructure, where nonequilibrium phonons driven by a temperature gradient transfer their angular momentum to electron spins via interfacial phonon-spin conversion. Using the nonequilibrium Green's function formalism, we derive an expression for the injected spin current and show that it depends on the difference between the contributions from the two phonon branches with opposite circular polarizations. We further investigate the temperature dependence of the injected spin current density at different in-plane magnetic field strengths. In the superconducting state, the spin current density increases with temperature or in-plane magnetic field strength. In addition to the kink at the superconducting transition, a second kink appears below the transition temperature. The position of this kink is consistent with the onset of phonon-induced two-quasiparticle excitations as the superconducting gap decreases with increasing temperature. We further investigate the magnetic-field dependence of the kink temperature in a temperature--magnetic-field phase diagram.

title: Electrostatic and magnetic control of the anomalous Josephson phase in ferromagnetic hybrid junctions
summary: We report phase-sensitive measurements of Josephson junctions formed in InAs nanowires with epitaxial ferromagnetic EuS and superconducting Al shells. Using a superconducting interferometer, we observe a continuous, hysteretic anomalous phase shift under axial magnetic-field sweeps. A remanent phase bias persists at zero applied field and depends on magnetic history. Electrostatic gating strongly modifies the magnitude of the phase response, revealing its sensitivity to the transverse electronic structure of the nanowire. Self-consistent electrostatic simulations show that the effective Rashba spin-orbit coupling follows the measured gate-dependent phase response, suggesting its central role in the electrostatic control of the anomalous Josephson phase.

title: Thermal-energy relaxation in chiral quantum Hall edge mode
summary: We study the nonequilibrium state generated by a real Ohmic contact (ROC) in the charge-fractionalization regime. We then investigate its thermal-energy relaxation along a quantum Hall edge mediated by a fictitious Ohmic contact (FOC) with large capacitance and perfect coupling to the edge. For cold Ohmic contacts, the electron distribution function and current noise are fully described by their equilibrium forms and the corresponding Fermi-Dirac distribution. In contrast, in the case of hot Ohmic contacts, strong thermalization effects do not drive the outgoing state into complete equilibrium. Both the distribution function and the noise retain signatures of the initial nonequilibrium state and therefore cannot be characterized solely by the effective contact temperature, contrary to common assumptions.

title: Universal Analytical Description of Magnetoexcitons in Two-Dimensional Semiconducting Materials
summary: Matching the Coulomb and logarithmic limits of the Rytova--Keldysh model gives a universal zero-field spectrum for monolayer exciton $s$ states, $E_n\simeq-\mathrm{Ry}^*/[n-1/2+f_n(ξ)]^2$, where $ξ$ is the screening parameter. Analytical radii determine diamagnetic coefficients and the magnetic crossover scale. Zero-field deviations peak near $1\%$ across the full screening range $0\leqξ\leq100$. For the sampled hBN-encapsulated monolayers, magnetoexciton energies agree with numerical spectra to sub-meV rms up to $100\T$ and capture the measured orbital shifts. Shared parameters link optical and magneto-optical spectra.

title: Ultrastrong coupling between magnetoplasmons and higher cyclotron-resonance harmonics induced by spatially inhomogeneous electromagnetic fields in two-dimensional electron systems
summary: Finite-wave-vector electromagnetic fields provide a route to accessing nonlocal collective dynamics in two-dimensional electron systems. Here, we theoretically investigate the magnetoplasmon response of a two-dimensional electron system subjected to a spatially nonuniform electromagnetic field in a perpendicular magnetic field. By combining Maxwell's equations with the Kubo formula, we derive the nonlocal magnetoconductivity tensor and obtain the self-consistent dispersion relation for collective modes. We show that a finite in-plane wave vector enables higher-order cyclotron transitions, allowing higher harmonics of the cyclotron resonance to contribute to the nonlocal conductivity. These harmonics hybridize with the magnetoplasmon mode, producing avoided crossings in the collective-mode spectrum characteristic of Bernstein modes. To quantify this hybridization, we establish a correspondence between the Maxwell-Kubo dispersion relation and a Hopfield-type Hamiltonian and derive an analytical expression for the effective coupling strength between the magnetoplasmon and the n-th cyclotron-resonance harmonic. Our analysis reveals that the normalized coupling strength exhibits a nonmonotonic dependence on the in-plane wavelength, reaching a maximum that becomes nearly independent of electron density in the high-density regime. These results establish a quantitative connection between nonlocal magnetoconductivity, Bernstein-mode physics, and effective collective-mode coupling, providing design guidelines for realizing ultrastrong coupling in terahertz magnetoplasmonic systems.

title: Current-driven chiral RKKY interaction in altermagnets
summary: The Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya (DM) interaction between magnetic moments usually requires spin--orbit coupling and broken inversion symmetry. We show that in a spin-split metal without spin--orbit coupling a charge current generates a DM interaction between localized spins. Using Keldysh Green's functions (GFs) with a drifting Fermi sea, we compute the Ruderman--Kittel--Kasuya--Yosida (RKKY) interaction between two magnetic impurities in a two-dimensional $d$-wave altermagnet with an additional exchange splitting. To linear order in the current, the correction is a Fermi-surface term, and all its components are obtained in closed form in terms of Bessel functions, valid for arbitrary values of the two independent spin splittings, $β$ and $J_\perp$. The induced DM vector points along the spin-quantization axis, which in the present model is the out-of-plane direction $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$. At long distance it decays as $1/R$, one power more slowly than the equilibrium coupling. In the altermagnet it vanishes for bonds along the nodal directions, where the two spin bands are degenerate, and, for a diagonal current, has opposite signs on bonds along the two crystal axes. This $d$-wave signature reverses with the Néel vector and with the current, and distinguishes the altermagnet from a ferromagnet. The current also generates symmetric couplings that are odd in the impurity separation. In low-density two-dimensional conductors, the DM coupling can reach a few percent of the equilibrium exchange.

title: Field-Effect Magnon Transistor
summary: Antiferromagnetic magnons offer a promising platform for highspeed, energy-efficient information processing. Intrinsic odd-parity spin splitting in a cycloidal magnetic order offers a route to nonvanishing magnon transport in compensated magnets. Here, we propose a magnonic field-effect device (akin to a transistor) based on a ferroelectric antiferromagnet BiFeO3 in which a gate electric field reconfigures domain boundaries to amplify/modulate magnon transport. These boundaries switch the nonlocal inverse-spin-Hall response between low- and high-signal states, with a pronounced dependence on the direction of magnon propagation. Source-drain reversal, magnetic-field measurements, symmetry analysis, and first-principles calculations reveal nonreciprocal magnon transport associated with the reversal of spin angular momentum across the domain boundaries. Our results establish an electrically programmable, non-volatile magnon transistor.

title: Quadrupole Origin of the Orbital Hall Effect in an $sp^3$ Centrosymmetric Lattice: Robustness and Tunability under Disorder
summary: We investigate how disorder affects orbital Hall transport in the centrosymmetric spinless $sp^3$ tight-binding model on a square lattice, widely used as a minimal model for the orbital Hall effect [1]. In the pristine system, the intrinsic orbital Hall response is related to the quadrupolar orbital texture generated by $s$-$p$ hybridization. Using the Kubo-Bastin formalism expanded in Chebyshev polynomials, we analyze the effect of vacancies, orbital-dependent Anderson on-site disorder, and selective $V_{spσ}$-bond disorder on the orbital transport. For Anderson disorder and vacancies, the longitudinal charge conductivity decreases faster than the orbital Hall conductivity over the range studied, leading to an increase of the orbital Hall angle and, in the Anderson case, saturation at stronger disorder. Selective $V_{spσ}$-bond disorder behaves differently: by modifying only the $s$-$p$ hybridization channel while leaving the remaining hopping network intact, it can produce a non-monotonic orbital Hall response and enhance the orbital Hall conductivity at intermediate dilution. Overall, our results show that the orbital Hall response remains sizable under vacancy and on-site disorder, while selective modification of the $s$-$p$ hybridization provides an additional route to tune the orbital Hall conductivity.

title: Ferroelectric control of the $K$--$Γ$ valley landscape in R-stacked bilayer WSe$_2$
summary: In bilayer WSe2 the valence-band maxima at K and Γ lie within a few thermal energies of one another, and gating redistributes holes between a light and a heavy valley of different mobilities on a landscape that stays fixed. We show that rhombohedral (R) stacking moves the landscape itself. The three-fold symmetry of R stacking forbids interlayer tunneling at K but not at Γ. The K coupling is therefore exactly zero, not merely small. A fit that leaves the coupling free returns an upper bound of 0.017 meV, three orders of magnitude under k_BT at room temperature, while the Γ coupling is 361.8 meV. The polarization creates a potential step between the layers and splits the K doublet. Each K state stays on a single layer, so the K edge shifts by half of that splitting, 41.7 meV, which any tunneling would reduce. Γ barely responds. Two consequences follow from symmetry alone, whatever the size of that shift. The two registries, carrying opposite out-of-plane ferroelectric polarizations, are exact mirror images along the displacement-field axis, and reversing the polarization reverses the displacement of the landscape. Their differential-mode transconductances are equal and opposite at zero field, where the response vanishes for an ideal nonpolar reference. The stored polarization is read out as a reversal of sign and not as a difference of current. Sweeping the field is a second route to the same parity. In the ideal symmetric limit the transconductance passes through zero at the field that cancels the polarization, 1.07 V/nm, at a single temperature. Both routes are limited by the symmetry of the device more than by the band structure. Stacking also renormalizes the landscape, so the polar one is not a translated copy of the nonpolar reference. Absolute offsets follow the exchange-correlation functional. The symmetry relations do not.

title: State Diagram of Dual-Free-Layer Perpendicular Magnetic Tunnel Junctions for Artificial Spiking Neurons
summary: The performance of perpendicular magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) depends critically on interfacial properties and layer thicknesses, small variations of which can substantially modify their magnetic and transport characteristics. This work investigates, experimentally and numerically, a perpendicular MTJ with two free layers, a configuration that preserves the precessional dynamics of the device while simplifying its fabrication. Quasi-static state diagrams measured under magnetic fields and DC or pulsed bias reveal static parallel, antiparallel, and bistable regimes, as well as a dynamical windmill regime in which the reversal of one layer triggers that of the other, giving rise to spiking neuron-like signals. Macrospin simulations reproduce these diagrams, and a stability analysis of the Landau-Lifchitz-Gilbert (LLG) equation yields an analytical description of the critical lines, including the windmill threshold voltage. The comparison also reveals a quadratic term in the voltage dependence of the spin-transfer torque that Joule heating cannot explain. The analytical model shows that the threshold voltage can be lowered either by approaching the spin-reorientation transition, at the cost of thermal stability, or by enhancing the quadratic contribution to the spin-transfer torque. These results establish guidelines for optimizing multilayer MTJ stacks for artificial spiking neurons and a broader range of neuromorphic and spintronic applications.

title: Electrical transport of surface-bound electrons on annealed solid neon
summary: We study the dc transport of electrons bound to the surface of solid neon using the conventional Sommer-Tanner method. First, we find that the capacitive cross-talk for the thickness of solid samples on the order of a millimeter varies substantially with the temperature and is strongly affected by the sample annealing. Second, we find that, even for the annealed samples, the observed response of electrons differs significantly from that of the surface-bound electrons on liquid helium and cannot be satisfactorily described by conventional models. Despite this, we managed to extract the resistance of the electron system from its in-phase response and investigate the temperature dependence in a wide range between 1.4 and 20 K. In a high-temperature range between 16 and 20 K, the resistance behavior is found to agree very well with the vapor-atom scattering mechanism, while at lower temperatures it is consistent with temperature-dependent scattering by surface roughness. Our analysis indicates a high electron mobility of electrons on solid neon but two orders of magnitude lower density than expected. These results suggest surface electrons as a suitable probe for studying the morphology of the neon surface but call for a better understanding of the experimental method applicable to such systems.

title: Theory of anisotropic magnetotransport beyond the constant relaxation-time approximation in multi-Weyl semimetals
summary: Multi-Weyl semimetals, characterized by Weyl nodes carrying higher monopole charges, provide a platform for exploring topological magnetotransport beyond the conventional Weyl paradigm. Here, we develop a generalized semiclassical Boltzmann framework for multi-Weyl semimetals with arbitrary monopole charge $N$, incorporating the orbital magnetic moment (OMM) into the quasiparticle dispersion and Berry-curvature-modified dynamics, together with a momentum-dependent collision integral accounting for intra- and intervalley scattering. We investigate the longitudinal magnetoconductivity (LMC) and planar Hall conductivity (PHC) for $N=1$, $2$, and $3$, considering both nonmagnetic and magnetic impurity scattering. In the absence of OMM, the LMC remains positive and quadratic in the magnetic field throughout the investigated scattering regime, consistent with conventional chiral-anomaly-assisted transport. Including OMM, however, leads to a sign reversal of the LMC under sufficiently strong intervalley scattering for the $σ_0$ and $σ_z$ impurity channels. Remarkably, the critical intervalley scattering strength decreases systematically with increasing monopole charge, indicating an enhanced tendency toward negative LMC in higher-charge Weyl systems. Furthermore, we find that the PHC also undergoes a sign reversal for $N=2$ and $N=3$ in the same impurity channels, while remaining positive for $N=1$ within the investigated parameter range. The angular dependences retain their characteristic $\sin^2γ$-like and $\sin2γ$ profiles for LMC and PHC, respectively, even across the sign reversal. Our results demonstrate that the interplay of Berry curvature, OMM, monopole charge, and impurity scattering can produce qualitatively distinct weak-field magnetotransport responses beyond the conventional chiral-anomaly picture.

title: Exciton-polarons in monolayer semiconductors with drifting electrons
summary: Recent work has demonstrated that the optical absorption of moderately doped two-dimensional semiconductors can be described in terms of exciton-polarons. In this picture, interactions between a photoexcited exciton and a Fermi sea of excess charge carriers split the exciton spectrum into a lower-energy attractive polaron branch and a higher-energy repulsive polaron branch. Due to the negligible in-plane momentum of photons, however, optical measurements probe only exciton-polarons near zero momentum, leaving their finite-momentum physics largely unexplored. Here we propose accessing this regime by measuring the absorption in the presence of an electric bias current. In effect, this displaces the electronic Fermi sea in momentum space, such that an optically active exciton-polaron at rest acquires finite momentum relative to the charge carriers. Using a diagrammatic formulation of the exciton-polaron problem, we derive exact relations between the spectral and quasiparticle properties of current-biased exciton-polarons and their finite-momentum counterparts in an equilibrium Fermi sea. These relations show that absorption measurements with drifting electrons can reconstruct the momentum dependence of the quasiparticle properties for both branches. We estimate that experimentally accessible currents can probe a broad momentum range while remaining within the linear-response regime.

title: Optical spin Edelstein response of d-wave altermagnets
summary: The momentum-dependent spin splitting and compensated magnetic order in altermagnets offer opportunities for electrical control of spin polarization. We explore the spin Edelstein effect in the frequency domain of a two-dimensional d-wave altermagnet with Rashba spin-orbit coupling. We calculate the spin-velocity susceptibility response function beyond the intraband response regime and find that the interband longitudinal and transverse Edelstein responses are governed by the Zeeman quantum metric and Zeeman Berry curvature, respectively. The density of states presents a logarithmic van Hove singularity at exactly the negative value of the energy below which four disconnected Fermi contours emerge. This defines three distinctive regions for the position of the Fermi level, through which the Edelstein susceptibility tensor displays characteristic spectral features, reflecting the topological change of the Fermi surface. The resulting spin magnetization shows a strong dependence on the driving frequency and on the orientation of the in-plane external electric field. Our results highlight new possibilities for electrical and optical control of the spin Edelstein effect in altermagnets that could find spintronic applications.

title: Strain-Engineering Giant Pseudo-Electric Fields in Multilayer Graphene
summary: Electromagnetic scalar and vector potentials can be engineered in solids through lattice distortions, providing a versatile means of tuning electronic band structures. The pseudovector component, which generates pseudo-magnetic fields, has received much attention for its ability to realize a zero-field quantum Hall effect. However, the pseudoscalar component, giving rise to pseudo-electric fields to which many electronic systems are intrinsically susceptible, has not yet been experimentally explored. Here, we demonstrate the emergence and profound consequences of the pseudoscalar potential in a multilayer graphene system. Atomic relaxation reconstructs the system into large Bernalstacked domains separated by one-dimensional rhombohedral channels. Within this inter-dimensional system, we achieve the first direct atomic-scale imaging of distinct lattice deformations in graphene under strain. In rhombohedral channels, we observe that the tensile lattice deformation induces giant pseudo-electric fields, producing ultra-flat dispersion with divergent density of states and a large energy gap. This results in enhanced electronic correlations, leading to flat-band instabilities and striped modulation in the density of states that would otherwise require strong external displacement fields. Moreover, the gap opened by the pseudoscalar potential protects topological boundary states that persist in the absence of applied fields. Our results provide a comprehensive atomic-scale characterization of graphene elasticity and direct spectroscopic evidence for the nontrivial pseudo-electric field arising from lattice distortion. More broadly, it provides an intrinsic and tunable pathway to new quantum states

title: Optical writing of Dzyaloshinskii Néel-type skyrmions
summary: Ultrashort laser pulses offer a route to write nanoscale topological magnetic textures for information processing. Magnetic skyrmions are prototypical examples, yet optically generating them with controlled position, type, and, in particular, chirality remains challenging. This challenge arises because magnetic dipolar interactions, which often drive skyrmion formation, preserve the degeneracy between opposite chiralities, leaving no uniquely selected spin configuration. Here, we show that in an ultrathin Co/Pt film, sequences of picosecond circularly polarized laser pulses can write Néel-type, fixed-chirality skyrmions stabilized solely by the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction. Combining Lorentz transmission electron microscopy and magneto-optical microscopy, we comprehensively reconstruct their internal spin structure across multiple length scales, ranging from nanometres to micrometers. Using asymmetric skyrmion-expansion measurements, we determined the sign and magnitude of the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and identified the written chirality. Our findings connect deterministic optical writing with the controlled spin structure of skyrmions, advancing optical control of topological textures for opto-spintronic applications.

title: Interaction Landscapes of Structurally Distorted Toroidal Classical Spin Textures
comment: to appear in Adv. Theory Simul
summary: We develop a classical discrete magnetostatic model of localized magnetic moments arranged in a toroidal texture, where the moments are represented by static current loops and study the behavior of the magnetic dipole-dipole interaction under several types of structural deformations. The purpose is to disentangle effects due to geometric and magnetic deformations, including elliptical, lopsided, alternating, and tilted configurations. In particular, we investigate how distortions modify the toroidal moment and the interaction energy between pairs of toroidal structures. The resulting interaction landscapes exhibit characteristic symmetry patterns and anisotropies that are highly sensitive to the underlying deformation. As a separate proof-of-concept comparison, first-principles calculations on a molecular spin-toroidal system reveal qualitatively similar orientation-dependent behavior. The calculated interaction is microscopically the conventional pairwise magnetic dipole-dipole interaction between localized moments arranged in a spin-toroidal texture; the toroidal moment characterizes the collective texture and should not be interpreted as introducing an additional elementary interaction term. Our results provide a platform for exploring orientation-dependent interactions of spin-toroidal textures in molecular magnets and related nanoscale magnetic systems that are essential to understand the role of toroidal order.

title: Torsional Hall Viscosity of Massive Chern Insulators: Finite Temperature and Chemical Potential
summary: We study the torsional Hall viscosity $ζ_{\rm H}$ of Chern insulators at finite temperature and chemical potential. Our analysis considers the massive Dirac fermion and two deformations: a constant out-of-plane magnetic field and a momentum-dependent mass described by the single-block Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang (BHZ) Hamiltonian. For the massive Dirac theory, we show that temperature and chemical potential lead to UV-finite corrections and that a chemical potential outside the bulk gap modifies $ζ_{\rm H}$ even at zero temperature. In a constant magnetic field, the response of massive Dirac fermions is dictated by the relativistic Landau-level spectrum, leading to a plateau structure at zero temperature that is smoothed at finite temperature. The jumps are proportional to the Dirac mass and inversely proportional to the squared magnetic length and the newly occupied Landau-level energy. Finally, we present a detailed study of the correction to $ζ_{\rm H}$ in the single-block BHZ continuum model due to temperature and chemical potential. For parameters relevant to (Hg,Mn)Te quantum wells, the magnitude of the jump across a mass domain wall retains its vacuum enhancement due to the BHZ deformation as long as the chemical potential lies sufficiently deep inside the gap compared with the thermal energy. Our results extend the theory of torsional Hall viscosity to experimentally relevant conditions and may facilitate its future detection.

title: Low-energy states of a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain connected perpendicularly to a metallic lead
summary: Recently, Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chains (SSHCs) coupled to metallic leads have attracted attention. In particular Martínez {\it et al.} [Phys. Rev. Res. {\bf 8}, 043118 (2026)] studied a topological SSHC connected at one of its ends perpendicularly to a metallic lead modeled by a tight-binding chain. Here, we extend their results by incorporating the finite-size splitting of the end modes of the isolated SSHC, which are determined analytically with high accuracy. We also derive simple analytical expressions, valid in the low-energy regime, for the zero-temperature conductance through the lead and the relevant spectral densities. We find that, when the chemical potential coincides with that of the half-filled SSHC, the conductance reaches its maximum value, equal to that of the lead in the absence of the SSHC. By contrast, the conductance vanishes when the chemical potential is shifted by an amount equal to half the end-mode splitting.

title: Vortex states in submicron titanomagnetite particles
summary: Numerical simulation is used to study the magnetic properties of spheroidal titanomagnetite particles Fe(3-x)TixO4 (0.4 < x < 0.6) with semi-axes ratio ranging from 0.5 to 1.5 and transverse diameters D = 100 - 480 nm. It is shown that various vortex micromagnetic states can emerge in the titanomagnetite particles depending on the titanium concentration, aspect ratio and particle diameter. The single-domain particle diameters are determined using the energy diagrams for stationary uniform and vortex states. The remanent magnetization of dilute assemblies of titanomagnetite particles with varying titanium content are calculated as a function of the transverse particle diameter D. It is demonstrated that for submicron-sized titanomagnetite particles, D ~ 500 nm, the normalized remanent magnetization of the assembly reaches very low values, M/Ms < 0.01, where Ms is the saturation magnetization of the particles.

title: Energy spectrum of trions in semiconductors
summary: Energy levels of trions in a bulk semiconductor crystal are calculated by two different numerical methods. On the one hand, we construct the finite-element solution of the Schrödinger equation in the total angular momentum representation. On the other hand, we use the Gaussian expansion method (GEM), applied to each of the three Faddeev components of the wave function. The results for the total angular momenta $J=0$ and $J=1$ of the trion were obtained for a wide range of the hole-to-electron mass ratios covering most existing semiconductor compounds. The dependencies of the energies on the mass ratio for trions in a bulk crystal qualitatively agree with the results for a simplified model of a trion in a 1D quantum wire, for which the three-body energies can be calculated with arbitrary precision as well as easily approximated using Born-Oppenheimer potential-energy curves. A comparison of our results with data from other publicly available three-body codes as well as with the energies of well-known atomic counterparts, in particular, with vibrational energy levels of the molecular hydrogen ion, shows a good agreement and confirms the accuracy of the numerical data. We found that GEM significantly improves the precision of the obtained trion energies compared to previous calculations. Our calculations demonstrate that, for most semiconductor compounds, only one trion state with zero total angular momentum exists.

title: Electrostatic and magnetic control of the anomalous Josephson phase in ferromagnetic hybrid junctions
summary: We report phase-sensitive measurements of Josephson junctions formed in InAs nanowires with epitaxial ferromagnetic EuS and superconducting Al shells. Using a superconducting interferometer, we observe a continuous, hysteretic anomalous phase shift under axial magnetic-field sweeps. A remanent phase bias persists at zero applied field and depends on magnetic history. Electrostatic gating strongly modifies the magnitude of the phase response, revealing its sensitivity to the transverse electronic structure of the nanowire. Self-consistent electrostatic simulations show that the effective Rashba spin-orbit coupling follows the measured gate-dependent phase response, suggesting its central role in the electrostatic control of the anomalous Josephson phase.

title: Double quantum dots as dynamical impurities in one-dimensional transport
summary: We study single-electron scattering in a tight-binding chain capacitively coupled to double quantum dots, which act as dynamical two-level-system impurities with electrically tunable level splittings. For a single impurity, we solve the scattering problem exactly and show Feshbach-like perfect elastic reflection, whose resonant condition distinguishes the initial two-level state. For several impurities in a strongly reflecting chain, transmission peaks at an intermediate mean level splitting. At small splittings, energy exchange with the impurities can weaken constructive interference between backscattered paths, consistent with the initial rise in transmission. As excitation channels close, virtual transitions can enhance reflection and drive transmission below its purely elastic value $T_0$. At larger splittings, these virtual processes weaken and transmission approaches $T_0$. We discuss how gate-controlled transmission measurements in quantum-dot arrays could test these predictions.
